Aethiopia Celestia — From ancient heritage to the next frontier.

We're an Ethiopian team bringing together technology, creativity, and curiosity about space. We're joining NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to explore NASA's open data and build an innovative solution. We're looking for motivated teammates interested in web development, Python, data analysis, mapping/GIS, Earth or planetary science, UI/UX design, and storytelling. All skill levels are welcome!
summary:
FarmShield is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform designed to help African farmers make informed, location-based farming and crop-rotation decisions.

It combines climate information from NASA POWER, rainfall data from CHIRPS, soil information from SoilGrids, and agricultural knowledge to help users understand local farming conditions. Through an interactive map, users can explore locations, examine environmental information, and evaluate crop and crop-rotation options.

FarmShield uses an explainable, rule-based recommendation system rather than machine learning. It aims to make scientific information more accessible, support sustainable farming practices, and help farming communities adapt to changing environmental conditions.

Our goal is to connect Earth observation and agricultural science with practical decisions that support more resilient agriculture across Africa.
details:
What does your project do, and how does it work?

FarmShield is a web-based platform that aims to make agricultural information easier to understand and use. We started with Ethiopia, with the goal of supporting more climate-resilient farming across Africa.

With FarmShield, users can explore different countries and farming locations through an interactive map. They can view the environmental information available for a location and compare different crops and crop-rotation options.

To support these decisions, we bring together climate information from NASA POWER, rainfall data from CHIRPS, soil information from SoilGrids, and agricultural knowledge. Since not all data is available everywhere, FarmShield aims to clearly show whether information is live, historical, modelled, reference-based, or unavailable.

FarmShield also includes a rule-based crop-rotation recommendation system. Instead of using machine learning, it considers five factors: climate suitability, soil suitability, water requirements, biological nitrogen fixation, and botanical family diversity. These factors are used to calculate a suitability score that helps users compare options. The score is intended to support decision-making, not to predict or guarantee crop yields.

What benefits does it have?

FarmShield brings useful environmental and agricultural information into one place. It helps users understand the conditions in a selected location and compare crop-rotation options before making farming decisions. By presenting the factors behind each recommendation, it also makes the results easier to understand.

What is the intended impact?

We hope FarmShield can help farmers, agricultural experts, and researchers make better-informed decisions. In the long term, we want to encourage sustainable farming practices, improve access to environmental information, and contribute to more climate-resilient agriculture across Africa.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

We built the frontend using React and TypeScript to create the interactive user interface. For the backend, we used Python and Flask to handle the application logic and data services. SQLite is used for development data storage, while Leaflet powers the interactive maps.

How is your project creative?

What makes FarmShield different is the way it brings together climate, rainfall, soil, and agricultural information in one platform. Rather than simply displaying data, it uses an explainable rule-based approach to show how different environmental factors can influence crop-rotation choices.

What factors did your team consider?

Our recommendation system considers five factors, each with a different contribution to the final suitability score:

  1. Climate suitability – 25%
  2. Soil suitability – 25%
  3. Water requirements – 25%
  4. Biological nitrogen fixation – 15%
  5. Botanical family diversity – 10%

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

During the development of FarmShield, our team used AI-assisted tools, including ChatGPT and Antigravity, to support software development, coding, debugging, troubleshooting, and project documentation.

These tools helped us work through technical challenges, improve parts of the code, and refine our documentation. Our team guided the project direction, made the development decisions, and designed the explainable, rule-based crop-rotation recommendation system.

AI tools were not used to generate or fabricate NASA observations or scientific measurements.
